ana: quick signal from nightly long-seq run on mistral-7b (AWQ int8) — p95 latency jumped 1.8x at seq=2048 compared to fp16, throughput dropped ~2.3x :thinking:
bench-bot: nightly-summary: model=mistral-7b-awq quant=awq-int8 seq=2048 batch=1 p50=210ms p95=890ms throughput=1.1toks/s accuracy_delta=-0.6%
chris: can you paste the profiler output? curious which kernel fell back
ana: pasted below — main callsites show matmul_int8_fast for the first 512 tokens, then matmul_fp16_fallback afterward. KV cache hitrate also drops after token ~600 (we see repeated kv_rebuild events)
ana: ```
[PROFILE] kernel_select: matmul_int8_fast 0-512
[PROFILE] kernel_select: matmul_fp16_fallback 513-2048
[PROFILE] kv_cache: hits=0.71 misses=0.29 evictions=14 rebuilds=3
[LOG] latency_p95=890ms
```
lee: that pattern smells like RoPE scaling / head-dim mismatch triggering kernel guardrails. AWQ quant for this model reduces weight dynamic range and the int8 matmul kernel has stricter scale checks so it bails to fp16 when estimates exceed threshold :eyes:
zach: did you run with rope_scale=1.0? we recently changed default rope_cutoff heuristics which can interact with kv shard tiling
ana: default rope_scale=1.0. tried rope_scale=0.95 as a quick test — reduced fallbacks but accuracy dropped for some prompts (we saw hallucination on long repeat patterns)
chris: can you repro locally? share the exact bench command
ana: repro cmd: `./run_bench --model mistral-7b-awq --quant awq-int8 --seq-len 2048 --batch 1 --rope-scale 1.0 --profile=/tmp/prof.json`
lee: one mitigation: force the int8-safe kernel variant that has relaxed guard (slower than matmul_int8_fast but faster than fp16 fallback). env override: `REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE=matmul_int8_safe` or per-model config: `{
  "kernel_policy": {"mistral-7b-awq": "matmul_int8_safe"},
  "batching": {"max_batch": 8, "microbatch_ms": 10}
}`
zach: also try tweak batching heuristics — for long seqs big batch accumulation causes memory churn + kv eviction. lowering max_batch to 8 reduced evictions in our internal run
chris: what about recalibrating AWQ? maybe the calibration prompts were too short and the quant scales are off for long-context tokens
ana: good call. original calib used 256-token prompts sampled from webtext. I re-ran calib with 1024-token prompts including repeated-entity sequences. accuracy delta improved from -0.6% -> -0.15% but p95 still ~1.3x fp16
zach: possible that the AWQ per-channel scales cross the int8-kernel guard threshold occasionally for high-token-index heads due to RoPE scaled queries — kernel then emits fallback which is expensive. We should add a small fast path: detect rope_scale mismatch early and apply a per-request kernel hint
lee: logging idea: emit `kernel_hint=INT8_SAFE` when estimated q_scale > 0.9*guard. That would avoid the costly probe and fallback. cheap to add in runtime
ana: created a quick patch branch with hint logic and kernel override toggle, ran a quick pass — p95 improved from 890ms -> 720ms, throughput ~1.6toks/s. will push PR once tests clean

zach: also add a calibration recipe note: include at least 10% long-seq (>=1024) and repeated-token patterns to AWQ calibration set for Mistral family
